prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map places the camera wearer’s floral-covered torso/lap in the lower foreground at roughly 0.2–0.5 m, with the extended forearm and hand about 0.3–0.7 m away and the pan, food, and work surface farther ahead at roughly 0.6–1.2 m. The torso lies below and partly occludes the surface, while the arm projects from the right toward the upper-left/upper-center area and overlaps the pan region; the pale round object at far left is partly outside the view. Across the five frames, the hand shifts rightward and slightly away from the pan while the major surfaces remain at nearly constant depth, indicating mostly arm/camera rotation rather than strong approach or retreat. Brightness clarifies near–far layering that is ambiguous in RGB, but the very bright garment, merged boundaries, and smooth halos suggest unreliable metric scale and depth bleeding around the arm, torso, and pan.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates one person region—principally the visible arm/hand—above and to the right of the camera wearer’s foreground torso, plus intermittently detected food or vessel regions labeled “pizza,” “cake,” and “clock.” These detected objects lie immediately beside or beneath the hand, plausibly within about 0.3–0.8 m of the camera wearer and within the visible person’s arm reach; their mutual separations are generally under about 0.5 m. Over time, the person mask moves from upper-center/right toward the far right while the object masks appear, disappear, or change class, so the map supports lateral motion and overlap but not dependable approach, facing direction, gaze, or behind/in-front ordering. It exposes object extents and occlusions more clearly than RGB, but labels such as “clock,” the fused “pizzaperson” text, inconsistent cake masks, missing torso/table regions, and small detached person fragments are visibly unreliable.
descriptions.pose: The pose map consistently places a magenta hand near the upper-middle or upper-right, matching the hand working above the pan; it remains roughly 0.4–0.8 m from the camera wearer and close to the nearby food/vessel region. From frames 2–5 the hand shifts rightward and changes orientation, while finger landmarks rotate and spread, making hand pose and turning easier to see than in RGB. A yellow body skeleton appears only in frame 5, extending from left/center toward the hand at the right, but it does not provide enough stable head or facial landmarks to determine which way a person faces or whether anyone looks toward the camera wearer. The missing body pose in frames 1–4, distorted hand geometry, disconnected yellow points, and skeleton segments crossing mostly empty image areas make body position, occlusion, reach, and absolute distance unreliable beyond the hand’s approximate location.
